subject: Dedicated capacity follow-up: proposed GPU mix, throughput & $/1M token target
body:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@medlytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity follow-up: proposed GPU mix, throughput & $/1M token target

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can produce a formal reserved-capacity quote that matches MedLytics' unit-econ target.

What I captured from our conversation:
- Workload: real-time clinical triage assistant + nightly batch indexing for model updates.
- Traffic profile: 1. baseline steady-state ~250k tokens/day, 2. peak burst windows 18:00-20:00 PST with estimated concurrency up to ~60 concurrent sessions (avg 80 tokens/resp), 3. nightly batch ~10M tokens (non-latency sensitive).
- Desired SLOs: p95 gen latency <= 450ms for short requests (<=128 tokens); batch can be scheduled.
- Target unit economics: MedLytics is aiming for ~$120 / 1M tokens (to fit forecasted margins). You said budget range for the Dedicated tier is roughly $90k–$150k/month depending on SKU and support.

Proposed sizing assumptions (for discussion):
- GPU mix options:
  * H100 x4 + A100 x4 (mixed pool) — better for peak short-latency bursts and throughput density on heavy models
  * A100 x8 (homogenous) — simpler ops, lower per-GPU list cost, slightly lower peak throughput for short latencies
- Reserved capacity: 8 GPUs initial commitment (we can scope pilots at 4 GPUs for 30 days)
- Estimated throughput targets: 60 concurrent requests at p95 <=450ms maps to ~6–8 tokens/ms sustained across the pool (subject to model selection + quantization).
- Economics: with our batching + prefix/KV caching we project $95–$140 / 1M tokens depending on serialization (float16 vs 4-bit quant) and effective batching.

Next steps I need from you to finalize the quote:
1) Confirm the budget band you want us to prioritize for pricing (lower band -> A100-only; upper band -> H100-mixed).
2) Confirm peak concurrency target (is 60 concurrent concurrent sessions the right upper bound? do you expect spikes above that?)
3) Share any compliance or networking constraints for the Private/Dedicated deployment (VPC, inbound IP allowlists, KMS).

I've attached a short capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx with per-GPU cost rollups and a GPU_throughput_matrix.pdf with our rough latency/throughput tradeoffs for the two SKU mixes.

If it helps, we can hop on a 20-minute call tomorrow to align on the concurrency math and which SKU to price first.

Thanks —

Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142
Redwood Inference

---

From: Asha Patel <asha@medlytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medlytics.com
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity follow-up: proposed GPU mix, throughput & $/1M token target

Hi Hannah —

Appreciate the recap. Quick answers below:
- Budget: we want to stay within $100k–$130k/month ideally. We can stretch to $150k if the unit econ clearly hits the margin target and SLAs are locked.
- Concurrency: 60 is our expected steady peak. We anticipate rare spikes to ~85 for a few minutes during new release days. If you can model a graceful fallback for spikes (e.g., auto-burst to hosted tier or queued low-priority requests) that would be ideal.
- Compliance: standard SOC2 + HIPAA controls are required; we use a customer-managed KMS and require audit logs retention for 12 months.
- $/1M tokens target: Our finance lead is looking for a realized cost closer to $110 / 1M tokens after batching and average-case caching.

Please proceed with two pricing paths: (A) A100-only 8x reserved, (B) mixed H100/A100 4+4 reserved. Include pilot option (4 GPUs for 30 days) and an explicit spike-handling plan.

Thanks —

Asha
Head of Product, MedLytics
asha@medlytics.com

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity follow-up: proposed GPU mix, throughput & $/1M token target

Hannah/Marissa —

Quick internal note after Asha's reply:
- Target realized cost $110 / 1M tokens -> we should price both paths to show an achievable midpoint.
- Spike handling: propose canary burst lane (2-host H100 on burst) + automatic fallback to hosted API at an agreed throttling policy. Need ops to confirm feasibility and stability for HIPAA workloads.
- For SOC2/HIPAA + customer KMS, mark this as Private deployment requirement (no multi-tenant hosted mix).

Action items: Marissa to draft private-deployment addendum + compliance checklist; Hannah to produce two path quotes and explicit pilot contract language.

- Ben

---

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@medlytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, procurement@medlytics.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity follow-up: proposed GPU mix, throughput & $/1M token target

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the clarity — this is perfect. We will:
- Send formal quotes for both pricing paths (A100-only 8x reserved; mixed H100/A100 4+4 reserved) by EOD Tuesday. Quotes will include: monthly cost, projected $/1M tokens (mid/low/high scenarios), pilot 4-GPU 30-day terms, and a spike/fallback operational appendix.
- Marissa will attach the HIPAA + KMS compliance rider in the quote bundle.
- I'll include recommended quantization and batching profiles we used to produce the $/1M projections so Finance can validate assumptions.

Can you confirm procurement contact for the DocuSign? I see procurement@medlytics.com on copy — if that's the right inbox I'll route signature links there.

Meeting availability: I have an open 20-minute slot tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT if you'd like to run the concurrency math quickly.

Best,

Hannah
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
